newsitem.title: USA: Gillette expects $1 bln cap-ex in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Gillette expects $1 bln cap-ex in 1997.

text.p: Gillette told analysts on Friday after reporting higher earnings it expects to spend $1 billion on capital expenditures in 1997.

Gillette spokesman Everett Howe said the $1 billion would be spent on all the company's divisions, including its recent acquisiton of Duracell and the razor and personal care giant expects to introduce "at least 20 new products" in 1997.
Howe said acquisition costs of $65 million, which involve investment banker fees and attorney costs, were higher than expected.
"The one-time charges associated with the merger amounted to $413 million on a pre-tax basis or $283 million after tax with an earnings per share impact of 51 cents," Howe said.

"These one time charges relate to restructing programs and other unusal, non-recurring items and $65 million consisting primarily of transaction costs for investment bankers' fees, attorneys' fees, accountants' fees, filings and other related charges.
"These merger-related costs are higher than our initial estimate of $340 million and are a function of identifying more cost savings opportunities during our due diligence work," Howe said.

He said he anticipated annual cost savings through "the combination of Gillette and Duracell will be greater than originally estimated, thereby generating a favorable return on the increase in one-time charges."
